result.rationale: In zoho-bigin CalendarService the diff replaces the direct axios.post with refreshOAuthTokens(...). In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), which has no `.data` property, yet the code immediately reads `tokenInfo.data.error`. So in sharing mode `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and accessing `.error` throws, breaking the token refresh. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: In sharing mode tokenInfo is the sync endpoint's fetch Response but the code reads `tokenInfo.data.error` expecting the axios response shape, and Response.data is undefined, so the access throws TypeError. Every Zoho Bigin token refresh in sharing mode crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)', failing the operation; the sync response body is never parsed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is now obtained via `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When sharing mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a `Response` object (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). The Zoho Bigin code still treats `tokenInfo` like an Axios response and accesses `tokenInfo.data.error`, but `Response` has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and reading `.error` will throw. The response body is also never parsed in this path.
